Mike Waltz: “President Trump has a plan for peace in Gaza. All sides - Hamas and Israel - need to abide by their commitments to it. The alternative is an endless cycle of violence and destruction.” I don’t think Israel and Hamas should be put on equal footing. But Israel is now facing VERY STRONG pressure from the Board of Peace to take 2 steps before Hamas disarms. The Board wants Israel to sign an agreement allowing an international force into Gaza and let Palestinian police recruits who passed Israeli background checks leave Gaza for training and return. Neither step requires Israeli troops to withdraw. The Board says it needs people on the ground to receive the weapons and verify that Hamas gives them up. If Hamas breaks its word, the Board says it will call it out publicly and act. I’m 99% sure Hamas will refuse to disarm, and I trust President Trump to stand by Israel on security. Israel should let the Board put Hamas to the test. If Hamas refuses, everyone will see who broke the deal, and Israel will be justified in taking the task of disarming Hamas themselves. (This will probably be the case) If Israel has security reasons to hold off, it should explain them VERY clearly and PUBLICLY now. A fight with Washington over this is avoidable. We don’t need a new PR nightmare.

A Europa League fixture between Beşiktaş and "Israel's" Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was interrupted by police violence after Turkish supporters unfurled banners calling for freedom for Palestine. One banner read, "Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine," prompting police to violently enter the stands with batons and pepper spray. The clashes forced a 30-minute suspension of the match. Georgia's Interior Ministry claimed that UEFA representatives, rather than Georgian officials, took the Palestinian flags from supporters, but offered no explanation for the police intervention. Before kickoff, Beşiktaş players refused to shake hands with their Israeli opponents. The Istanbul side eventually secured a 2–1 victory through two late goals.
